svg.aria-label: MIB-NB fields and the 640 ms NPBCH cycle
svg.title: MIB-NB fields and the 640 ms NPBCH cycle
svg.text: The MIB-NB: 34 bits, and how I find where its 640 ms cycle begins
bits reconstructed from the decoded values (my decoder prints values, not raw bits)
top 4 bits (12) here; the low 6 bits (14) are where I am inside the 640 ms cycle: 12·64 + 14 = 782
low 2 bits of the hyperframe number; SIB1 adds the high 8 (0x51 = 81): 81·4 + 3 = 327
SIB1-NB is 208 bits long and sent 16 times per 2.56 s; with an even PCI it starts in frame 0
a version number; it changes when the cell edits its SIBs, so a meter knows when to re-read
not inside an LTE carrier: no LTE control region or CRS to skip, the whole 180 kHz is NB-IoT
The NPBCH cycle: 64 frames = 8 blocks × 8 frames. Each block is one eighth of the codeword, repeated 8 times
The problem: when I start listening I do not know which of the 64 frames I am in, and the frame number is inside the message I am trying to read.
So I guess. For every hypothesis "frame 0 of the cycle was o frames ago" (32 offsets, because NSSS already told me even/odd),
× 1 or 2 antenna ports × Rel-13 or Rel-14 rotation = 128 guesses, I stack my frames into the right block slots and run Viterbi + CRC.
Only the right guess passes the CRC-16 (with the port mask). If two pass, I keep the one whose re-encoded bits match the received ones best.
Winner: Rel-14 rotation, 1 port, offset such that my newest frame is frame 14 of the cycle (all of block 0 + 7 frames of block 1), NPBCH SNR 13.9 dB.
Frame 14 of the cycle with SFN-MSB 12: 12 × 64 + 14 = 782. Only frames from the same cycle can be added, which is why it says 15 frames.
